notes:
BOTH RED BEATS STAYED RED. John 10 is Jesus teaching in the flesh and a
red-letter KJV inks both.
  j1  John 10:7  'Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep.'
  j2  John 10:9  'I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved...'

FRAMING SPLIT ADDED. John 10:7 in the KJV reads 'Then said Jesus unto them again,
Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep.' The opening clause is
John writing, not Jesus speaking, and a red-letter Bible leaves it black. It is now
its own segment:
  s7  John 10:7  'Then said Jesus unto them again,'  SCRIPTURE, blue.
s7 and j1 sit on the SAME still (ST2) - consecutive beats over one image, no new
artwork, and the edit the viewer sees is unchanged.

LIFTED: n1a paraphrased 'anyone who climbs in some other way is there to take, not
to care.' That is Jesus's own sentence, John 10:1, and it opens the whole
sheepfold teaching. Added verbatim, JESUS red:
  j0  John 10:1  'Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door
      into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and
      a robber.'
n1a keeps its original text and now works as the retelling right after it, on ST3
- the wall-and-the-door still, which is exactly what the verse describes.

BEAT ORDER: j0 (John 10:1) now runs before j1 (John 10:7), which is the order John
wrote them in and the order the picture logic already wanted - the wall first, then
the door. Every original id is kept; only j0 and s7 are new.

WOMEN: John 10 records no woman speaking. Nothing added; nothing invented.

WHY-LAW: a sheepfold had one opening and the shepherd lay down across it at night -
he WAS the door. Milk framing - the door is not a barrier keeping you out, it is the
one place you can go in and out freely and still be safe.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus used a picture the crowd knew well — a sheepfold with one opening, and a shepherd who guards it.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Anyone who climbs in some other way is there to take, not to care.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Then said Jesus unto them again,

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the door? The door lets the flock in safe.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Through Him you come in and you go out — free, fed, not trapped. He's the way in, and the way to everything good.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There's one door. Knock, and walk through.

stills_wanted.ST2: ST2 now carries John's framing line AND 'I am the door of the sheep.' Frame the declaration: Jesus standing in the single gap of a low stone sheepfold wall at dusk, filling the opening, sheep settled behind him. He is not pointing at the door. He is standing in it.
stills_wanted.ST3: ST3 now carries John 10:1 verbatim and its retelling. Frame the wrong way in: a figure hauling himself over the top of the stone wall in the dark, off to one side, while the real opening sits plainly visible further along. Furtive, hurried, taking - and the door is right there, unused.
